This will get you hungry. Not right away, but once you get to a point where you're demanding that your body respond, well... your body will respond.

Definitely don't start out very heavy, you don't want to hurt yourself. But once you get some weight on the bar and start using the lower body muscles your body will start to release hormones, you will change a little bit. Your body is an ecosystem. If you stay sedated and sedentary, well your body will (and seems like it is) respond to that. Start asking it to do other things and it will get better at those other things.

Also what you eat, and when you eat, plays a major role in these things as well. I like to carb up in the morning, like steel cut oats or quinoa, and that gives the body some energy. Then concentrate on green things, fruit, and protein for the rest of the day, keeping carbs super low.

Eating foods heavy in simple carbs and/or sugar are pretty terrible for keeping your metabolism going, I don't touch the stuff. The exception is fruit, it does have fructose but it also has some great fiber.

Back to powerlifting, this is a really great read here: http://stronglifts.com/5x5/

The beginning is super light, takes 15 minutes maybe, and definitely isn't going to get you dizzy. Next session is just a little bit more, and the session after that is also just a little bit more. Take it how you feel, you'll know what to expect.

You really need to change your diet. Carbs like pasta and rice are really not that great for you and the common knowledge surrounding them is under a lot of scrutiny currently. Eating more animal proteins and green plants should give you the energy to work-out and let your body repair itself. Sometimes our bodies forget what they need and default to listening to a bacteria that lives in our gut, which often becomes addicted to carbs. Eating healthier for a few weeks should wake your body up to what it needs and make you crave the food thats actually giving you fuel. If your not eating some days at all, you need to set a schedule and stick to it. Prepare some food in advance (I usually just buy a rotisserie chicken at the supermarket and hard boil some eggs) so that you have something that requires little effort to eat if you're feeling lazy.
